cards.b: The prime mover: the muscle that contracts to produce movement.
The muscle that relaxes (lengthens) to allow the agonist to move the joint.
Strong, inelastic tissue attaching muscle to bone.
Biceps and triceps: biceps flex the elbow, triceps extend it.
Hip flexors (flex the hip) and gluteals (extend the hip).
Deltoid (raises the arm) and latissimus dorsi (pulls it down and back).
Upper back and neck muscle; raises the shoulders and pulls the shoulder blades together.
Chest muscles that pull the arm across the body, e.g. in a bench press.
Stomach muscles that flex the trunk and hold posture and core stability.
Isotonic contraction where the muscle shortens, e.g. biceps lifting in a bicep curl.
Isotonic contraction where the muscle lengthens under control, e.g. lowering into a squat.
The muscle contracts without changing length and there is no movement, e.g. a plank.
Slow: low force, fatigue-resistant, aerobic (marathon). Fast: high force, fatigue quickly, anaerobic (sprint).

gaps.s: The muscle that relaxes while the agonist contracts is called the ___.
The muscle on the front of the thigh that extends the knee is the ___ group.
In an eccentric contraction the muscle ___ while it contracts.
Holding a plank is an ___ contraction.
The calf muscle that causes plantar flexion is the ___.
___ twitch fibres resist fatigue and use aerobic energy.
The muscle at the top of the shoulder that raises the arm is the ___.

short.q: A footballer kicks a ball. Name the agonist and antagonist at the knee.
short.model: The quadriceps are the agonist, contracting to extend the knee. The hamstrings are the antagonist and relax.

short.q: Explain the difference between concentric and eccentric contractions using the biceps.
short.model: In a concentric contraction the biceps shortens as the weight is lifted. In an eccentric contraction the biceps lengthens under tension as the weight is lowered.

short.q: Why do sprinters have mostly fast twitch fibres?
short.model: Fast twitch fibres produce high force and use anaerobic energy, which suits a short, explosive sprint. Fatigue does not matter in about 10 seconds.
points: Anaerobic, short duration so fatigue irrelevant

short.q: Name the muscles used for a sit-up and for pushing up onto tiptoes.
short.model: The abdominals perform the sit-up and the gastrocnemius works in plantar flexion to rise onto the toes.

short.q: Describe the roles of the hip flexors and gluteals in sprinting.
short.model: The hip flexors lift the knee forward as the leg swings through. The gluteals extend the hip, driving the leg back and propelling the sprinter forward.
points: Hip flexors flex hip / lift knee
Gluteals extend hip / drive the leg back
